jobs.description: With about 15,000 students, more than 300 professorships and around 160 degree programs, the RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau is the technical university of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate. As a place of top international research, it offers excellent working conditions and career opportunities. Those who study, research or work at RPTU experience a cosmopolitan environment and shape the future.As part of the DFG-funded project Energy Structures: Energy Sustains Dissipative Structures in Soil Systems (https://soilsystems.net/projects-partners/2-p1-energy-structures/), the RPTU in Landau and the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) in Leipzig jointly offer a PhD position.Place of work: 50% at RPTU in Landau (32.5%) and 50% at UFZ in Leipzig (32.5%), according to agreement and project requirementsYour area of responsibility:The aim of the project is to understand how and under which conditions carbon and energy are transformed and stored in soils. Through incubation experiments and thermodynamic modelling, you will quantify matter and energy fluxes and characterize their efficiency and limitations. In doing so, you will investigate how energy inputs from organic substrates affect dissipative processes in soil microbial communities and whether dissipative structures develop in soils that govern matter and energy fluxes and thereby promote soil carbon storage.To achieve this aim, you will primarily work with a newly developed calorespirometric system at RPTU in Landau, which you will also further develop. In Leipzig, you will work with a newly developed plug-flow reaction calorimeter at UFZ. The measurements will be complemented by key chemical and biological analyses of the soil and its microbial community, including isothermal microcalorimetry (IMC), thermogravimetry–differential scanning calorimetry–quadrupole mass spectrometry (TG-DSC-QMS), phospholipid fatty acid (PLFA) analyses, elemental analyses and molecular biological analyses.The project is part of the DFG Priority Programme SPP 2322 SoilSystems (https://soilsystems.net/). You will benefit from the interdisciplinary collaboration within the programme's nationwide research consortium. Close collaboration, in particular with Trier University, is also planned.We offer:- Top-level research at the interface between research centre and university, with an excellent reputation nationally and internationally- The opportunity to benefit from the expertise of two research institutions- Excellent technical infrastructure and equipment- Work in interdisciplinary and international teams- Excellent connections to national and international research networks- Comprehensive support and optimal training courses by our graduate schools (HIGRADE at UFZ and ZGaPL at RPTU)- Salary according to the German public sector pay scale TVöD/TV-L, pay grade E13 (65%)Your requirements profile:- Master's degree or equivalent in soil science, environmental sciences, biochemistry, biology, chemistry, or a related field- Strong interest in complex and interdisciplinary processes in soil systems- Interest, willingness and ability to integrate new scientific concepts into soil science research- Prior experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage, but not a prerequisite: soil science, environmental microbiology, calorimetry, and thermodynamics; Willingness to expand your expertise into complementary fields is expected- Curiosity and openness to learning new methods, critically evaluating and further developing existing approaches, and exploring new methodological solutions- Willingness to independently learn new methods, troubleshoot and develop creative solutions to methodological challenges- Openness to incorporating modelling approaches and aspects of microbial ecology into your research- Willingness to work in an interdisciplinary and international team- Very good written and spoken English skillsMore informations given on our homepage:https://jobs.rptu.de/jobposting/f03b170329d9425cfa5355ad0c4fe4ba72fea9bb0 (https://jobs.rptu.de/jobposting/f03b170329d9425cfa5355ad0c4fe4ba72fea9bb0)We look forward to receiving your detailed application (CV, references, etc.) by 15.11.2026 at the latest.The job interviews are scheduled to take place in calendar weeks 48 and 49.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholdsThe work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: Oneof the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain abetter understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles ofnature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as itprovides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physicsdeals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Amongthose hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the protonand the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created viacollisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 yearsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-15Your tasks:- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolutionstudies within LHCb data analysis.- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scatteringamplitudes.- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS / amplitude-serialization format.- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.- Exchange with the experimental collaborations [LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.Your profile:- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity with quantum field theory and scattering theory.- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with version control and reproducible workflows.- Very good command of written and spoken English.- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and inopen, reusable research software.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA)
